:::{#rem-generalization-error}
#### Other names, and how the expected error splits

@hastie2009elements [sec. 7.2] also call $\generr_{\trainset}$ the *test error*,
and in sec. 7.12 the *conditional* test error.
It is the [risk](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-risk)
of the prediction $\fitted(\newpredvar)$
under the [loss](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-loss-function) $\loss$,
computed with the training set held fixed.

The argument $\nobs$ of the [expected generalization error](#def-expected-generalization-error)
$\expgenerr{\fitproc}{\nobs}$ of a fitting procedure $\fitproc$
records that it depends on how many observations each training set has.
By @thm-expected-error-epe, $\expgenerr{\fitproc}{\nobs}$ averages
the expected prediction error at each covariate value,
and @thm-epe-decomposition splits each of those expected prediction errors,
under squared-error loss,
into a squared bias, a variance and a noise variance.

:::
